references.text: The original command from God to Moses to make dishes, bowls, pitchers and basins of pure gold for the table of showbread.
The instruction to place the showbread on the table, for which these utensils were intended.
The description of the table of showbread itself, to which these utensils belong.
Mentions the dishes, bowls, cups and pitchers that were used on the table of showbread when the Levites packed them for transport.
Silver dishes and gold bowls given as offerings to the sanctuary, similar to the utensils in the tabernacle.
Solomon made similar utensils of gold for the temple, including the table for the showbread and accompanying dishes and bowls.
Describes the utensils that Solomon made for God's house, including the tables and golden vessels.
The Babylonians took the bowls, fire pans, basins and other utensils of gold and silver from the temple.
Hebrews mentions the table and the showbread in the first tabernacle as part of the sanctuary of the old covenant.
Theological continuity: Solomon's temple takes over and confirms the requirement for golden vessels found in the books of Moses.
Fulfillment of pattern: Solomon's temple restores the specific golden utensils from the books of Moses.
